To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the coordination of Zn ions by tau causes a conformational change in the DNA-binding region which results in a switch from minor groove binding mode to major groove binding mode.

1) DNA-binding mode of 4R tau undergoes transition upon binding to Zn ions, and 2) DNA-binding mode transition of 4Rtau is induced by Zn ions via coordination of Zn by cysteine residues located in MTBD.
the DNA-binding mode of 2N/ 4R tau undergoes transition in the presence of zinc ions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of Zn on the DNA binding properties of tau.
the effect of Zn ions on DNA-binding mode of 2N/ 4R tau.
the effects of Zn ions on the DNA-binding properties of 4R tau.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Zn ions cause a conformational change in the DNA-binding region of tau protein and change the mode of tau–DNA interaction from minor groove binding in the absence of Zn ions to major groove binding when Zn ions are present in the system.

tau binds to the minor groove of DNA via PRD and MTBD in the absence of Zn ions and in the presence of 1:1 tau:Zn stoichiometry, tau undergoes a conformational transition and binds to the major groove via PRD and the last repeat (R4) of MTBD.

the presence of Zn causes a conformational change in tau and leads to a switch in the DNA-binding mode from minor groove binding in the absence of Zn to major groove binding mode in the presence of 1:1 molar ratio of Zn ions to tau.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Zn coordination causes tau aggregation in vitro which is a key step in tau toxicity in vivo.
tau–DNA interaction is a Zn-sensitive process and Zn ions can modulate tau–DNA interaction.
tau protein can bind to DNA in two different modes, minor groove binding and major groove binding, and the presence of Zn causes transition between these two modes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Zn ions can induce conformational change in tau protein and cause transition from minor groove to major groove binding mode.
coordination of Zn to cysteine residues changes the DNA-binding mode of MTBD from minor groove to major groove.
coordination of Zn by tau induces tau aggregation and causes tau to switch its DNA-binding mode from minor groove binding into major groove binding.
